q: Which scheduling algorithm gives the minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes that are all available at the same time?
exp: SJF is provably optimal for minimizing average waiting time.

q: Memory has free partitions of 100, 500, 200, 300 and 600 KB (in order). Processes of 212, 417, 112 and 426 KB arrive in that order. Which strategy can place all four processes?
exp: Best fit: 212→300, 417→500, 112→200, 426→600. First fit and worst fit leave 426 KB unplaced.

q: A 16 GB disk has 4 KB blocks. A bit-vector (bitmap) is used for free-space management with one bit per block. What is the size of the bitmap?
exp: Blocks = 2^34 / 2^12 = 2^22 bits = 2^19 bytes = 512 KB.

q: What is the key difference between a mutex and a binary semaphore?
options: A mutex has ownership: only the thread that locked it should unlock it
A binary semaphore cannot be used for signalling
A mutex can take any non-negative integer value
A mutex is used only between processes
exp: Mutexes are owned by the locking thread, whereas a binary semaphore can be signalled by a different thread.

q: Which statement about shell redirection is correct?
options: > overwrites the target file whereas >> appends to it
Both read input from the file
exp: cmd > f truncates f first; cmd >> f appends output at the end.

q: The Banker's algorithm is an example of:
exp: Banker's algorithm checks that each allocation leaves the system in a safe state before granting it.

q: In demand paging, a page-table entry whose valid-invalid bit is "invalid" means that the page:
options: is not in main memory (or is not part of the process address space)
exp: An invalid bit signals that the page is not currently in physical memory (or the address is illegal). Access causes a trap; if the page is legal, the OS brings it in (page fault).

q: A process that has finished execution but still has an entry in the process table because its parent has not yet called wait() is known as a:
exp: A terminated child whose exit status has not been collected by the parent remains as a zombie.

q: What is the average rotational latency of a disk rotating at 7200 RPM?
exp: One rotation = 60/7200 s = 8.33 ms; the average latency is half of that, 4.17 ms.

q: Match the system with its category: (i) VxWorks (ii) MS-DOS (iii) UNIX. Which mapping is correct?
options: (i) single-user OS, (ii) multi-user OS, (iii) real-time OS
(i) Real-time OS, (ii) single-user single-tasking OS, (iii) multi-user multitasking OS
(i) real-time OS, (ii) multi-user OS, (iii) single-user OS
(i) multi-user OS, (ii) real-time OS, (iii) single-user OS
exp: VxWorks is an RTOS, MS-DOS ran one task at a time for one user, and UNIX supports many users and processes.

q: In a microkernel design:
options: all OS services including file systems and drivers run in kernel space
there is no kernel at all
applications run in kernel mode for speed
only minimal services (IPC, basic scheduling, memory management) run in kernel space and other services run in user space
exp: A microkernel keeps the kernel small; the cost is extra message-passing overhead between user-space servers.

q: In segmentation with paging (as in MULTICS and Intel x86 designs):
options: each page is divided into segments
each segment is divided into pages
the whole process is kept in one contiguous segment
exp: Paging each segment removes the external-fragmentation problem of pure segmentation while keeping the programmer's logical view and sharing/protection benefits.

q: Starvation of low-priority processes in priority scheduling is commonly solved by:
exp: Aging gradually raises the priority of a process that has waited long, ensuring it eventually runs.

q: External fragmentation in contiguous memory allocation can be reduced by:
exp: Compaction shuffles processes to merge scattered free holes into one large block.

q: Which directory structure allows a file to be shared among users without making copies, but needs care to avoid dangling references?
options: Simple tree directory with no links
exp: Acyclic-graph directories permit shared files or subdirectories through links.

q: In the dining philosophers problem with five philosophers and five chopsticks, which approach avoids deadlock?
options: Give each philosopher a time quantum
Let philosophers eat in parallel without any lock
Let every philosopher pick up the left chopstick first and then the right one
Allow at most four philosophers to sit at the table at the same time
exp: If every philosopher grabs the left chopstick, circular wait occurs; limiting to four ensures at least one can get two chopsticks.

q: RAID level 1 provides fault tolerance by:
options: mirroring the data on two disks
exp: RAID 1 writes identical copies to two disks (100% capacity overhead). RAID 0 is striping without redundancy; RAID 5 uses distributed parity.

q: Deadlock can be prevented by breaking circular wait through:
options: allowing processes to hold resources while waiting
imposing a total ordering on resource types and requesting resources in that order
exp: If every process requests resources in increasing order of number, a cycle cannot form.

q: Reference string: 1,2,3,2,1,4,5,2,1,2,3,4 with 4 frames and LRU. How many page faults occur?
Which transition is NOT possible in the standard five-state process model?
exp: A ready process is not running, so it cannot issue an I/O request; only a running process can move to waiting.

q: If the time quantum in Round Robin scheduling is made extremely large, the algorithm behaves like:
exp: If the quantum exceeds every burst, no process is preempted and processes run in arrival order.

q: A disk has 4 surfaces, 1024 tracks per surface, 64 sectors per track and 512 bytes per sector. What is its capacity?
The UNIX operating system was originally developed at:
exp: Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie developed UNIX at Bell Labs around 1969-1971.

q: The exec() family of system calls:
options: waits for the child to finish
replaces the current process image with a new program while keeping the same PID
exp: exec loads a new program into the calling process's address space; no new process is created.

q:
Statement I: Paging eliminates external fragmentation.
Statement II: Pure segmentation suffers mainly from internal fragmentation.
Which option is correct?
exp: Paging uses fixed-size frames so there is no external fragmentation; segmentation uses variable sizes and suffers external fragmentation.

q: A file of size 10 KB is stored on a disk with 4 KB blocks. How much space is lost to internal fragmentation?
exp: 3 blocks (12 KB) are used for 10 KB of data, so 2 KB is wasted in the last block.

q: In a Round Robin system the time quantum is 2 ms and each context switch takes 0.5 ms. What is the CPU efficiency (useful fraction of time)?
A spinlock is most appropriate when:
options: the waiting threads should sleep to save power
there is only one CPU and the holder is not running
the lock is expected to be held for a very short time on a multiprocessor
the lock will be held for several seconds
exp: Spinning wastes CPU, so it pays off only when the wait is shorter than a context switch.

q: Which command creates a symbolic (soft) link named mylink pointing to the file data.txt?
exp: ln -s TARGET LINKNAME creates a symbolic link; without -s a hard link is made.

q: The 'ostrich algorithm' for deadlocks means:
options: ignoring the problem and assuming it rarely occurs
using the Banker's algorithm at each request
exp: Systems like UNIX and Windows largely ignore deadlock because prevention and detection are costly.

q: What is 'cycle stealing' in DMA?
options: The CPU takes extra clock cycles from the DMA
The DMA controller takes the memory bus for a few cycles, delaying the CPU
Instruction cycles are skipped to save power
Two processes share one CPU cycle
exp: In cycle-stealing mode, DMA transfers one word at a time by briefly taking over the bus.

q: In the one-to-one multithreading model:
options: all user threads share a single kernel thread
kernel threads are created only for the main thread
user threads cannot run in parallel on multiprocessors
each user thread maps to its own kernel thread, so one blocking call does not block the others
exp: One-to-one (Linux, Windows) gives true parallelism on multiprocessors and avoids blocking the entire process, at the cost of creating a kernel thread per user thread.

q: Which interprocess communication mechanism is generally the fastest once it has been set up?
exp: After setup, shared memory accesses need no system calls or kernel copying, unlike message passing.

q: A disk has average seek time 6 ms, rotates at 6000 RPM and has 100 sectors per track. What is the average time to read one sector?
exp: Rotation = 10 ms; average latency 5 ms; transfer = 10/100 = 0.1 ms; total = 6 + 5 + 0.1 = 11.1 ms.

q: Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
exp: Firefox is a web browser application; the others are operating systems.

q: An inverted page table has:
options: one entry for each logical page of every process
one entry for each physical frame
one entry for each disk block
one entry for each TLB line only
exp: It is indexed by frame and stores (process id, page number), reducing table size at the cost of search time.

q: In the FAT file system, the information about the next block of a file is found in:
options: the File Allocation Table entry for the current block
the first byte of the block itself
exp: The FAT stores a chain of cluster numbers; each entry points to the next cluster or an end-of-file marker.

q: Which of the following scheduling algorithms is inherently non-preemptive?
exp: FCFS lets a process run until it finishes or blocks; the others can preempt a running process.

q: Semaphore x is initialised to 0. Process P1 executes: S1; signal(x). Process P2 executes: wait(x); S2. What is guaranteed?
options: S1 and S2 execute at the same time
exp: P2 blocks on wait(x) until P1 signals after S1, enforcing the order S1 then S2.

q: In the first readers-writers problem (readers have priority), the main risk is:
exp: If readers keep arriving, a writer may wait indefinitely because new readers are allowed in while others are reading. The second variant favours writers and can starve readers.
